message.content:
**Famous Dancers of the 19th Century**

| Name | Nationality | Notable Contributions |
|------|-------------|-----------------------|
| **Marie Taglioni** (1804–1884) | Swedish-Italian | Pioneered the “en pointe” technique; star of *La Sylphide* (1832). |
| **Jean Coralli** (1799–1868) | French | Co‑director of the Paris Opera Ballet; choreographed *Giselle* (1841). |
| **Marius Petipa** (1818–1910) | Russian | Master choreographer of the Imperial Russian Ballet; created *Swan Lake*, *The Sleeping Beauty*, and *The Nutcracker*. |
| **Carlo Blasis** (1815–1877) | Italian | Influential ballet teacher; authored *Principles of Classical Dance* (1855). |
| **Fanny Elssler** (1810–1884) | Austrian | Renowned Viennese ballerina known for her virtuosity and dramatic flair. |
| **Adeline Genée** (1859–1944) | Danish | Celebrated ballerina who performed across Europe and the United States. |
| **Anna Pavlova** (1881–1931) | Russian | Though born in the late 19th century, she rose to fame in the early 20th; known for *The Dying Swan*. |
| **John L. T. (John L. T.)** | American | Early American ballet dancer and choreographer; helped establish ballet in the U.S. |
| **Eugène Scribe** (1791–1861) | French | While primarily a playwright, his works inspired many ballets of the era. |
| **Giovanni Battista Viotti** (1755–1824) | Italian | Composer and violinist; his music was often used in ballets of the time. |

These dancers and choreographers shaped the evolution of ballet and dance during the 19th century, influencing both performance style and technical standards that continue to resonate today.
